# Sirach Chapter 51 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 51 | **Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## Council Notes

Sirach 51 is the book's epilogue, comprising two distinct poems: (1) a thanksgiving psalm for deliverance (vv. 1–12) and (2) an acrostic poem on the pursuit of Wisdom (vv. 13–30). The acrostic is visible in the Hebrew text (Qumran Cave 11 Psalms Scroll) where each line begins with a successive letter of the Hebrew alphabet; the Greek translation preserves the substance but loses the acrostic structure.

**Critical note on the acrostic poem (vv. 13–30):** The Hebrew text of the Qumran version (11QPsa col. 21) contains erotic overtones that the Greek significantly toned down. The Hebrew speaks of seeking Wisdom as one would seek a beloved woman, with imagery drawn from the Song of Songs. The Greek version is more restrained. SOPHIA translates the Greek as given but notes this textual history.

**Key decisions:**
- v. 1: "O Lord, O King" vs. "Lord and King" — Greek Kyrie basileu. Both are accurate. "O Lord, O King" (EMET) is more liturgical; "Lord and King" (LOGOS) is more concise.
- v. 6: "a false tale to the king" — the historical background of this slander episode is unknown but clearly autobiographical.
- v. 10: "Father of my lord" — the address "Father of my lord" for God is unusual; it may be "Father of my Lord" or "God, Father of my Lord" — preserving the ambiguity is important.
- v. 13: "before I went on my travels" — Ben Sira apparently traveled; this is one of the few personal details about him.
- v. 23: "the house of instruction" (bet midrash in Hebrew) — this is the earliest attestation of this famous institution; preserve the exact phrase.
- v. 25: "Buy for yourselves without money" — echoes Isa. 55:1 ("come, buy without price"). The echo is deliberate.
- v. 26: "Put your neck under the yoke" — wisdom's yoke, picked up by Jesus in Matt. 11:29–30 ("take my yoke upon you").

---

**51:1** I will give thanks to you, O Lord, O King, and I will praise you, O God my Savior; I give thanks to your name,

**51:2** for you have been my protector and helper and delivered my body from destruction, from the snare of a slanderous tongue, from lips that utter lies; and against those who stood against me you were my helper,

**51:3** and you saved me in the abundance of your mercy and for your name's sake, from grinding teeth about to devour me, from the hand of those who sought my life, from the many afflictions that came upon me,

**51:4** from the smothering fire on every side, from the midst of fire which I had not kindled,

**51:5** from the depth of the belly of Hades, from an unclean tongue and lying words —

**51:6** slander delivered to a king by a treacherous tongue. My soul drew near to death, and my life was close to the depths of Hades.

**51:7** They surrounded me on every side and there was no one to help; I looked for human help, and there was none.

**51:8** Then I called to mind your mercy, O Lord, and your work from everlasting; for you rescue those who wait for you and save them from the hand of their enemies.

**51:9** And I lifted up my prayer from the earth, and pleaded for deliverance from death.

**51:10** I called upon the Lord, Father of my lord: "Do not forsake me in the days of trouble, in the time of the arrogant when there is no help.

**51:11** I will praise your name continually and will sing praises with thanksgiving." And my prayer was heard,

**51:12** for you saved me from destruction and delivered me from the evil time. Therefore I will give thanks and praise to you and bless the name of the Lord.

**51:13** When I was young, before I went on my travels, I sought wisdom openly in my prayer.

**51:14** Before the temple I prayed for her, and I will seek her to the end.

**51:15** From the first blossoming to the ripening of the fruit, my heart delighted in her; my foot walked the straight path; from my youth I have been on her track.

**51:16** I inclined my ear but a little and I received her, and I found for myself much instruction.

**51:17** I made progress in her; to him who gives wisdom I will give glory.

**51:18** For I purposed to live by her, I was zealous for the good, and I will not be put to shame.

**51:19** My soul wrestled toward her, and in my diligence I was confirmed. I stretched out my hands on high and mourned my ignorance of her.

**51:20** I directed my soul toward her, and through purity I found her; from the beginning I gained insight together with her; therefore I will not be forsaken.

**51:21** My heart was stirred to seek her; therefore I have gained a good possession.

**51:22** The Lord gave me my tongue as my reward, and I will praise him with it.

**51:23** Draw near to me, you who are uneducated, and lodge in the house of instruction.

**51:24** Why do you say you are lacking in these things, while your souls are so desperately thirsty?

**51:25** I opened my mouth and said: "Buy wisdom for yourselves without cost.

**51:26** Put your neck under her yoke, and let your soul receive instruction; she is near to find.

**51:27** See with your own eyes: I labored only a little and found for myself much rest.

**51:28** Acquire instruction as one would purchase much silver; through her you will gain gold in abundance.

**51:29** May your soul rejoice in his mercy, and may you not be put to shame in his praise.

**51:30** Do your work before the appointed time, and he will give you your reward in due season."
